title: Harry Maguire signs new Manchester United contract until at least 2027
content:
Harry Maguire has committed his future to Manchester United by signing a new one-year deal with the option of an additional 12 months.

The Athletic reported last month the England international was close to an agreement over a new deal with his previous contract having been set to expire at the end of this season.

The 33-year-old has become a mainstay of United’s line-up under Michael Carrick, starting all of the interim coach’s first 10 matches at charge prior to his red card against Bournemouth on March 20.

Upon signing the new deal, Maguire said: “Representing Manchester United is the ultimate honour. It is a responsibility that makes myself and my family proud every single day.

“I am delighted to extend my journey at this incredible club to at least eight seasons and continue to play in front of our special supporters to create more amazing moments together.

“You can feel the ambition and potential of this exciting squad. The determination throughout the whole club to fight for major trophies is clear for everyone to see and I am confident that our best moments together remain ahead of us.”

Maguire had impressed in a defensive four that United reverted to under Carrick, having previously played a 3-4-1-2 system under his predecessor, Ruben Amorim.

The former Leicester City defender had formed a central defensive partnership with Lisandro Martinez prior to the Argentina international’s injury, and subsequently with Leny Yoro. Matthijs de Ligt has been sidelined since early November.

The centre-back also returned to the England squad for the March friendly matches against Japan and Uruguay, ending his near two-year hiatus from the international setup.

Maguire was dropped from the England squad for Euro 2024 by previous coach Gareth Southgate after he failed to recover from a calf injury, and he was not selected for subsequent squads under interim coach Lee Carsley or his permanent successor Thomas Tuchel.

Analysis by Manchester United correspondent Andy Mitten

United have done the right thing by renewing Maguire’s contract.

Yes, the defender turned 33 in March, but it makes sense on several levels. He’s still a top-quality centre-back performing consistently for the club.

Replacing him would have cost tens of millions — money United need to prioritise on signings elsewhere in the team.

His form has been so impressive that he was recalled by England for their March internationals, having not been involved since September 2024. His dream of playing in the 2026 World Cup is not over.

Maguire is well respected in the United dressing room. Likeable, mature and settled, he connects well with staff and is seen as a positive influence on his peers.
